drug_profiles.name: Cabazitaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Binds tubulin, promotes microtubule assembly and inhibits depolymerisation, disrupting mitosis. Cabazitaxel was developed to retain activity in taxane-resistant tumour models.
drug_profiles.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

drug_profiles.name: nab-Paclitaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Delivers paclitaxel as albumin-bound nanoparticles. Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules and prevents normal depolymerisation, disrupting mitosis.
drug_profiles.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Post-docetaxel taxane plus continuous corticosteroid for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Cabazitaxel plus prednisolone is an NCCP regimen for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after docetaxel. v0.70.0 reconciles the executable rule layer to the current Version 8 source while keeping consultant and oncology-pharmacy validation pending.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with docetaxel
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Cabazitaxel stabilises microtubules and inhibits mitosis. Prednisolone provides the established corticosteroid component of the regimen.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cabazitaxel is administered on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle with continuous daily prednisolone. The source includes 25 mg/m² and an alternative 20 mg/m² cabazitaxel schedule.
key_points: 21-day IV taxane with continuous oral prednisolone
ANC and hepatic suitability are central
Gastrointestinal toxicity, neuropathy and renal failure require active review
Strong CYP3A interactions require medication reconciliation

Treatment-day haematology wording is source-sensitive: the NCCP count row joins ANC <1.5 with platelets <100; isolated ANC <1.5 is surfaced for clinician review rather than converting platelets <100 alone into a hold.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative systemic treatment intended to prolong survival and control disease.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and previous docetaxel exposure.
Continue appropriate androgen-deprivation strategy unless otherwise clinically directed.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG 0–2 in the NCCP eligibility section.
Review bilirubin/transaminases, renal status and interacting medicines.
important_cautions: Severe or recurrent gastrointestinal toxicity, neuropathy, renal failure and hypersensitivity can require dose modification or discontinuation.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Low in the central SACTCheck antiemetic mapping; use current NCCP antiemetic guidance together with the regimen-specific premedication schedule.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use the current regimen premedication including corticosteroid and hypersensitivity prophylaxis.
Consider G-CSF according to the NCCP risk pathway and prior neutropenic complications.
Provide early diarrhoea management and hydration advice.
patient_education: Report fever, severe diarrhoea, persistent vomiting, mucositis, neuropathy or reduced urine output promptly.
Review all new medicines for CYP3A interactions.
special_support: Maintain oral prednisolone continuity as prescribed.
Document the current cabazitaxel dose level and any previous toxicity-related reduction.

before_each_cycle: Diarrhoea, nausea/vomiting, stomatitis, neuropathy and hypersensitivity history.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Cabazitaxel Day 1 every 21 days with continuous daily prednisolone.
practical_workflow: Confirm ANC recovery and current dose before preparation.
Check hepatic category and clinically important CYP3A interactions.
Apply the exact NCCP adverse-event pathway after prior severe toxicity.
observation_and_access: Facilities to manage anaphylaxis must be available.
Use the current NCCP infusion and observation instructions.

evidence_audit.status: Two pass evidence audit completed for v0.70.0 source reconciliation
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: TROPIC provides pivotal post-docetaxel survival evidence; PROSELICA informs the 20 versus 25 mg/m² dose context; CARD provides later sequencing evidence after docetaxel and an androgen-signalling inhibitor.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: Foundational efficacy, dose-refinement and later sequencing evidence were reviewed.
remaining_uncertainties: Current NCCP treatment selection and dose modification remain authoritative.
Trial populations do not replace individual clinical suitability assessment.
Clarify with NCCP whether the treatment-day ANC <1.5 threshold is intended to act independently of the platelet criterion outside the baseline/recovery contexts.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First-line nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: nab-Paclitaxel plus gemcitabine is an NCCP first-line regimen for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. v0.70.0 adds the previously underrepresented Day 15 haematology branches and preserves source-permitted alternative strategies as clinician choices.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: nab-Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules while gemcitabine is a deoxycytidine analogue that inhibits DNA synthesis; the combination has phase 3 survival evidence.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: 28-day cycles with both drugs on Days 1, 8 and 15. Dose levels step from 125/1000 mg/m² to 100/800 mg/m² and 75/600 mg/m²; further required reduction leads to discontinuation under the source table.
key_points: Neuropathy and febrile neutropenia require active management
Day 15 options depend on the Day 8 action

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative first-line systemic treatment intended to improve disease control and survival.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma and first-line treatment context.
eligibility_orientation: Baseline ANC must meet the NCCP eligibility threshold.
Assess liver function and baseline neuropathy.
Review performance status, infection and marrow reserve.
important_cautions: The Day 15 table contains alternative strategies involving dose level and G-CSF; these require an explicit clinician decision.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Low in the current NCCP mapping; use national NCCP antiemetic guidance.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use G-CSF only where indicated by the source pathway and clinical context.
patient_education: Report fever, infection symptoms, neuropathy, rash, mucositis, diarrhoea or respiratory symptoms promptly.
special_support: Coordinate three treatment encounters within each 28-day cycle.
Document whether Day 8 was full dose, reduced or withheld before applying Day 15 guidance.

before_each_cycle: FBC before each scheduled treatment day as required.

practical_workflow: Identify the treatment day before interpreting counts.
For Day 15, explicitly record the Day 8 action before selecting a source-permitted option.
Track current dose level across both drugs.
observation_and_access: Use current NCCP infusion instructions and local venous-access procedures.

evidence_audit.status: Two pass evidence audit completed for v0.70.0 source reconciliation
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: MPACT provides the principal phase 3 evidence for the exact nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine schedule; longer follow-up supports persistence of the survival signal.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: Pivotal and mature follow-up evidence were checked.
remaining_uncertainties: Trial eligibility and performance-status selection must not be generalized beyond current NCCP clinical criteria.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Intensive first-line triplet chemotherapy plus bevacizumab for selected metastatic colorectal cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Bevacizumab plus FOLFOXIRI combines VEGF inhibition with irinotecan, oxaliplatin and infusional fluorouracil. v0.70.0 separates baseline from ongoing count thresholds, adds occurrence-specific dose pathways and corrects the bevacizumab proteinuria logic to the current NCCP source.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Metastatic colorectal cancer in a clinically selected population
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Bevacizumab inhibits VEGF-A signalling; irinotecan inhibits topoisomerase I; oxaliplatin forms DNA cross-links; fluorouracil inhibits thymidylate synthase and is modulated by folinic acid.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Day 1 every 14 days with bevacizumab, irinotecan, oxaliplatin/folinic acid and a 48-hour continuous fluorouracil infusion.
key_points: Baseline and ongoing blood-count thresholds differ
NCCP 00783 states an overall high emetogenic risk

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Palliative systemic treatment intended to improve disease control and survival.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Confirm metastatic colorectal cancer and clinical suitability for an intensive triplet backbone.
eligibility_orientation: ECOG ≤2 for adults under 70; ECOG 0 for ages 71–75 in the source.
Complete DPD testing before first fluorouracil exposure unless previously tested.
Review blood pressure, urine protein, bleeding/thrombosis, bowel disease and neuropathy.
important_cautions: Uncontrolled hypertension, proteinuria, bleeding/clotting risk and previous thromboembolic events require careful review.
Bowel obstruction/chronic bowel disease, complete DPD deficiency and bilirubin >3 ×ULN are source exclusions.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High: NCCP Regimen 00783 Version 2a explicitly states that the overall regimen poses a high risk of emesis.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: Use protocol prophylactic atropine unless contraindicated and manage irinotecan delayed diarrhoea promptly.
Provide DPD counselling when partial deficiency is identified.
patient_education: Start the instructed anti-diarrhoeal pathway promptly for delayed irinotecan diarrhoea and contact the service.
Avoid cold exposure around oxaliplatin and report laryngopharyngeal symptoms.
Report bleeding, severe headache, uncontrolled BP symptoms, wound-healing problems or thromboembolic symptoms.
special_support: Ambulatory infusion-pump pathway is required for the 48-hour fluorouracil infusion.
Coordinate proteinuria quantification when dipstick/laboratory screening triggers it.

baseline: Urine dipstick protein and blood pressure.
before_each_cycle: FBC, liver/renal profile, urine protein and blood pressure.
Peripheral neuropathy and gastrointestinal toxicity review.
Wound healing, bleeding/thrombotic events and other bevacizumab-specific toxicity.
priority_toxicities: Bevacizumab hypertension, proteinuria, bleeding, thrombosis and perforation

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Day 1 every 14 days; oxaliplatin precedes fluorouracil; fluorouracil is infused continuously over 48 hours.
route_and_duration: Bevacizumab infusion duration can shorten after tolerated initial infusions according to the source.
Oxaliplatin infusion may be prolonged for laryngopharyngeal dysaesthesia.
practical_workflow: Distinguish baseline from ongoing Day 1 assessment.
Record occurrence number for recurrent cytopenia because subsequent doses differ by occurrence.
Use component-specific bevacizumab hold/discontinuation criteria rather than reducing bevacizumab dose.
observation_and_access: Facilities to manage anaphylaxis must be available.
Ambulatory venous access/pump arrangements are required for continuous 5-FU.

evidence_audit.status: Two pass evidence audit completed for v0.70.0 source reconciliation
indications_reviewed: First-line treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer with FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab
evidence_audit.coverage_summary: TRIBE provides randomized evidence against FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab with mature survival follow-up; TRIBE2 tests an upfront/reintroduction triplet strategy against sequential doublets.
evidence_audit.later_or_add_on_search: Foundational randomized evidence, mature TRIBE survival and TRIBE2 strategy evidence were reviewed.
remaining_uncertainties: The regimen should remain restricted to clinically selected patients able to tolerate an intensive triplet strategy.
Molecularly targeted alternatives and sequencing depend on contemporary tumour biology and guideline context.

evidence_records.publication_title: Prednisone plus cabazitaxel or mitoxantrone for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing after docetaxel treatment
evidence_records.trial_population: 755 men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing during or after docetaxel-based treatment.
evidence_records.intervention: Cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² every 3 weeks plus prednisone 10 mg daily.
evidence_records.comparator: Mitoxantrone every 3 weeks plus prednisone 10 mg daily.
key_findings: Median overall survival was 15.1 months with cabazitaxel versus 12.7 months with mitoxantrone; hazard ratio for death 0.70.
The survival benefit established cabazitaxel activity after docetaxel, with clinically important neutropenia and gastrointestinal toxicity.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Pivotal randomized evidence supporting cabazitaxel after docetaxel in mCRPC.
evidence_records.limitations: The pivotal dose was 25 mg/m² and supportive-care practice has evolved. Current NCCP dosing, G-CSF and toxicity pathways remain authoritative.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact medicine and post-docetaxel disease setting
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Phase III Study Comparing a Reduced Dose of Cabazitaxel (20 mg/m²) and the Approved Dose (25 mg/m²) in Postdocetaxel mCRPC
evidence_records.trial_population: 1200 patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with docetaxel.
key_findings: Median overall survival was 13.4 months with 20 mg/m² and 14.5 months with 25 mg/m²; the prespecified non-inferiority criterion was met.
Grade 3–4 treatment-emergent adverse events were less frequent with 20 mg/m², while several secondary efficacy endpoints favoured 25 mg/m².
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Provides evidence context for the NCCP alternative 20 mg/m² schedule.
evidence_records.limitations: Non-inferiority was defined against retention of the TROPIC benefit and secondary efficacy endpoints favoured the higher dose; the NCCP source determines current dose selection.
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Cabazitaxel versus Abiraterone or Enzalutamide in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: Later-line mCRPC after docetaxel and progression on an androgen-signalling inhibitor
evidence_records.trial_population: 255 patients with mCRPC previously treated with docetaxel and an androgen-signalling-targeted inhibitor, with progression within 12 months on that inhibitor.
evidence_records.intervention: Cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² every 3 weeks plus prednisone and G-CSF.
evidence_records.comparator: The alternative androgen-signalling inhibitor (abiraterone or enzalutamide).
key_findings: Median imaging-based progression-free survival was 8.0 versus 3.7 months; hazard ratio 0.54.
Median overall survival was 13.6 versus 11.0 months; hazard ratio for death 0.64.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Important later sequencing evidence favouring cabazitaxel over switching to a second androgen-signalling inhibitor in the studied population.
evidence_records.limitations: This is a specific sequencing population and does not replace current NCCP selection criteria or broader contemporary prostate-cancer sequencing guidance.
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Increased survival in pancreatic cancer with nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine
evidence_records.trial_population: 861 patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer and Karnofsky performance status at least 70.
evidence_records.intervention: nab-Paclitaxel 125 mg/m² followed by gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 every 4 weeks.
key_findings: Median overall survival was 8.5 versus 6.7 months; hazard ratio for death 0.72.
Median progression-free survival was 5.5 versus 3.7 months; independently reviewed response rate was 23% versus 7%.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Pivotal phase 3 evidence for the exact combination and schedule family encoded in NCCP 00256.
evidence_records.limitations: The trial selected patients with Karnofsky performance status ≥70 and predates several modern pancreatic-cancer treatment developments.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact component combination, schedule and disease setting
evidence_records.review_status: Draft — consultant oncology and oncology-pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Initial therapy with FOLFOXIRI and bevacizumab for metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.trial_population: 508 patients with untreated metastatic colorectal cancer meeting the trial performance-status and age criteria.
key_findings: Median progression-free survival was 12.1 versus 9.7 months; hazard ratio 0.75.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Principal randomized evidence for upfront FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab versus FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab.
evidence_records.limitations: The trial used a clinically selected population and intensive therapy; current NCCP eligibility and toxicity management remain authoritative.
evidence_records.match_type: Exact triplet-plus-bevacizumab strategy and metastatic colorectal setting

evidence_records.publication_title: Upfront FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab and reintroduction after progression versus sequential doublets plus bevacizumab in metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.evidence_context: First-line and post-progression treatment strategy in unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer
evidence_records.study_design: Multicentre phase 3 randomised open-label strategy trial
evidence_records.trial_population: 679 previously untreated patients with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer.
evidence_records.intervention: Upfront FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab followed by reintroduction after progression.
evidence_records.comparator: mFOLFOX6 plus bevacizumab followed by FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab after progression.
key_findings: Median progression-free survival 2 was 19.2 versus 16.4 months; hazard ratio 0.74.
The intensified strategy produced more grade 3–4 diarrhoea and neutropenia during first-line treatment.
evidence_records.relevance_summary: Supports the clinical value of upfront triplet intensification and reintroduction strategy in selected patients.
evidence_records.limitations: TRIBE2 evaluated a treatment strategy extending beyond a single NCCP regimen cycle and showed increased toxicity; it must not create an automatic reintroduction pathway inside SACTCheck.
evidence_records.match_type: Contextual strategy evidence for the same first-line regimen
